newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Trade data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Trade data.

text.p: Following is a list of analysts' reactions to UK March global trade data and April non-EU trade figures published at 0830 GMT.
* UK MARCH GLOBAL TRADE DEFICIT 671 MLN STG (vs expectations deficit 900 million stg)
* UK APR NON-EU TRADE DEFICIT 335 MLN STG (vs expectations deficit 600 million stg)
CIBC CHIEF ECONOMIST DAVID COLEMAN - "Both figures are significantly better than expected ... On the headline numbers, suprisingly good numbers on both non-EU trade and global trade.

ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND ECONOMIST NEIL PARKER - "Better than forecast UK trade data should be stg positive, and slightly gilt and short stg negative. The March visible trade deficit at 671 million stg, and April non-EU deficit at 335 million both suggest a narrowing trade gap, something we don't expect to continue with sterling so strong.

BANK OF AMERICA ECONOMIST JEREMY HAWKINS - "The bottom lines to both the UK March global and April non-EU trade deficits were significantly smaller than expected. This should be positive for the pound. Global exports were soft but to the non-EU surged last month. Should help to ease some competitiveness worries so more reason for expectation the bounce in the pound will continue. Deficit with the EU was just 20 million stg in March. Given the relative strength of UK domestic demand, this bodes well for only a limited expansion medium term despite expected sustained sluggish growth in core Europe."
